result.title: Thinking Harder Doesn't Lead to Better Choices: Reasoning Effort Increases the Confidence but Not the Correctness of LLM Shopping Agents
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous shopping agents that process multimodal product listings (consisting of visual and text data) and recommend purchases on behalf of consumers. Naturally, one might assume that models with more thinking power would make higher-quality purchasing decisions. To test this belief, we ask two questions about such agents: does asking a model to think harder make it choose better products, and does the confidence it reports tell us the likelihood it may be wrong? We benchmark ten frontier models on three product-choice benchmarks built from WebShop, Amazon's SQID and Wayfair's WANDS platforms to see if LLMs with more thinking power actually make better-quality product purchase decisions. Across all three benchmarks, we found that increasing the thinking effort does not increase decision quality in a statistically meaningful way. The same change in thinking effort raises stated confidence at a statistically significant level, so extra thinking buys confidence rather than correctness. We also measure the calibration of these models (how well their reported confidence percentage matches their true correctness percentage) in these tasks and show that most models are not well-calibrated at every effort level. We also find that errors are strongly shared: when one model errs in a task, several others tend to err on that same task. Furthermore, on tasks where several models all err, a large number of them pick the same wrong product.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在基于 WebShop、SQID 与 WANDS 构建的三个多模态商品选择基准上评测十个前沿模型，检验提高推理努力是否提升购买决策质量、其自报置信度是否可信校准；结果显示更多思考不显著提升正确率，却显著抬高置信度，且多数模型校准普遍不佳、错误在不同模型间高度重合。
AI.relevance_reason: 这是一篇直接针对「THINK 的收益与成本」的负结果诊断，可为推理努力是否换取正确率、以及能否用自报置信度做停止或筛选证据的信号提供核查线索；但其衡量的是商品选择正确率，是否真正利用了图文证据中的视觉细节需读原文确认。
